tasks.problem_statement:
Kubernetes executor: per-poll unpaginated LIST events added in 19.4.0 saturates API Priority and Fairness on busy clusters

## Summary

19.4.0 added an unpaginated, unindexed `LIST` on `events` inside the pod-startup poll loop — [`checkPodSandboxUserNamespaceFailure`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/v19.4.0/executors/kubernetes/util.go#L263), called from [`getPodPhase`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/v19.4.0/executors/kubernetes/util.go#L225). It is controlled by `print_pod_warning_events`, which defaults to true, and fires once per poll interval (3s) for every pod that is not yet ready.

On a busy cluster with a shared runner namespace, each scan takes ~5 seconds — longer than the interval at which it is reissued. With hundreds of jobs in the startup phase this exhausted the API Priority and Fairness queues for the `service-accounts` flow schema, degrading all runner API traffic on the cluster and causing ~2.5 hours of elevated CI job failures across two production clusters. Rolling back to 19.3.2 resolved it immediately.

Every other Kubernetes API call added in this release is behind a feature flag. This one is not, so it shipped active to every Kubernetes executor installation. And for any installation without `FF_SUSPENDABLE_ENVIRONMENTS`, the scans **cannot** return a matching result — the work is unconditionally wasted. Both points are evidenced under [Possible fixes](#possible-fixes).

## Steps to reproduce

No special job definition is required. The call is in the pod-startup path, before the job script runs, so any job on the Kubernetes executor triggers it.

1. Run GitLab Runner 19.4.0 with the Kubernetes executor against a cluster whose runner namespace holds a large events collection. Ours holds ~5x10^5 event objects — simply what tens of thousands of jobs per day produce against the default one-hour event TTL, since each pod emits ~10-20 lifecycle events (`Scheduled`, `Pulling`/`Pulled`, `Created`, `Started` per container, secret and configMap mounts, teardown).
2. Leave `print_pod_warning_events` unset (defaults true) and `FF_SUSPENDABLE_ENVIRONMENTS` unset (defaults off).
3. Use a fixed runner namespace — `namespace_per_job = false`, the zero value.
4. Submit enough concurrent jobs that a meaningful number of pods are pending at once.
5. Observe on the API server:

```
sum(rate(apiserver_request_total{resource="events",verb="LIST",scope="namespace"}[5m])) by (code)
sum(rate(apiserver_flowcontrol_rejected_requests_total{priority_level="workload-low"}[5m])) by (reason)
histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(apiserver_request_duration_seconds_bucket{resource="events",verb="LIST",scope="namespace"}[5m])) by (le))
```

The events LIST rate steps up on deploy and returns to baseline on rollback to 19.3.2.

## Actual behavior

While a pod is pending, the runner issues one `LIST` on `events` per 3-second poll, scoped to the pod's namespace with `FieldSelector: involvedObject.name=<pod>,type=Warning`. The request carries no `Limit` and no `ResourceVersion`, and `involvedObject.name` is not an indexed field, so the API server performs a quorum range read over the namespace's entire events collection and filters server-side. The response is small; the read is not.

Measured against a ~5x10^5-object collection:

| `LIST events` duration | |
|---|---|
| p50 | **5,308 ms** |
| p90 | 7,342 ms |
| p99 | 9,541 ms |

Because the scan outlives its own poll interval, each job in the startup loop keeps more than one in flight continuously. This cost is inherent to the collection size rather than to the incident — the same call measured 8,877 ms mean the day *before* the upgrade, on 19.3.2, where it is reached only on the failure path. 19.4.0 did not make the scan slow; it moved an already-slow scan into the hot path and began issuing it continuously.

**Call rate** (`apiserver_request_total`, `resource=events, verb=LIST, scope=namespace`, core group):

| | baseline (19.3.2) | 19.4.0 | after rollback |
|---|---|---|---|
| cluster A, code 200 | 0.30-0.36/s | 2.31-3.07/s | 0.01-0.16/s |
| cluster A, code **429** | **0.00/s** | **0.51-1.92/s** | **0.00/s** |
| cluster B, code 200 | 0.32-0.46/s | 2.16-4.47/s | 0.19-0.29/s |
| cluster B, code **429** | **0.00/s** | **0.05-0.72/s** | **0.00/s** |

A square wave on both clusters independently, stepping up within one bucket of the deploy and collapsing on rollback. Up to ~36% of the scans were themselves rejected by the saturation they contributed to. The code [discards the error](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/v19.4.0/executors/kubernetes/util.go#L269), so none of this surfaced in job logs.

**API Priority and Fairness**, `service-accounts` → `workload-low`:

| | cluster A | cluster B |
|---|---|---|
| `queue-full` rejections, peak | 72.6/s | 42.2/s |
| `time-out` rejections, peak | 16.5/s | 9.6/s |
| peak `current_inqueue_requests` | 805 | 616 |
| `request_concurrency_limit` | 735 | 735 |
| peak `current_executing_requests` | 103 | 111 |

Requests were shed on **queue depth**, not seat exhaustion — seats peaked at 14% utilisation. That is the signature of a few slow requests holding queue slots, which is what a 5-second LIST is.

**Collateral damage.** `GET pods` is byte-identical between the two versions and neither its call count nor its response sizes changed, yet:

| | 19.4.0 | 19.3.2 baseline |
|---|---|---|
| `GET pods` mean duration | 1.11 s | 0.07 s |
| `LIST pods` mean duration | 0.78 s | 0.02 s |

Both are quorum reads sharing the same APF flow as the events scans, and both queued behind them. Since the pod GET's own code, count and payload are unchanged, the added latency is wait time.

**Feedback loop.** From `gitlab_runner_jobs` by `executor_stage`:

| `executor_stage=prepare`, by stage | change vs baseline |
|---|---|
| `state=pending` | 0 → hundreds |
| `prepare_script` | **8.6x** |
| `after_script` | **8.7x** |
| `cleanup_file_variables` | **6.8x** |
| `step_script` (actual build execution) | **0.8x** |

Stages that wait on the API server grew 6.8-8.7x while actual build execution *fell*. Jobs were not doing more work; they were accumulating in the phases that poll. Slower pod startup keeps jobs in the loop longer, which means more concurrent scans, which slows startup further.

**User-visible effect**, over the 2h25m window on the harder-hit of the two clusters: `runner_system_failure` rose from a 0.18% baseline to **13.69%**, and `job_execution_timeout` from 0.56% to 5.61%. Total job failure went from 8.74% to 26.58% — the baseline there is ordinary script failure, so the delta is the infrastructure-attributable part. Affected jobs stalled until killed by `activeDeadlineSeconds`, presenting to users as a job hung for the full timeout with no output.

## Expected behavior

Upgrading to 19.4.0 without enabling any new feature should not change the runner's Kubernetes API call pattern.

19.3.2 issues no events LIST on the pod-startup path. Its only events LIST is in [`logPodWarningEvents`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/v19.4.0/executors/kubernetes/kubernetes.go#L750), reached only from an error branch, and it sets [`Limit: 200`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/v19.4.0/executors/kubernetes/kubernetes.go#L759).

## Relevant logs and/or screenshots

The runner logs nothing for the LIST itself — the error is discarded at `util.go:269`. Everything below is downstream of the API server being saturated, and every terminal failure is timeout-shaped rather than naming a cause, which is what made this hard to attribute from the runner side:

<details>
<summary> job log </summary>

```sh
# Terminal failures seen by users — all timeout-shaped, none naming the events LIST:
ERROR: Job failed (system failure): couldn't get pod details: the server was unable to return a response in the time allotted, but may still be processing the request (get pods runner-<id>-project-<n>-concurrent-9-<hash>)  failure_reason=runner_system_failure
ERROR: Job failed (system failure): pod "<ns>/runner-<id>-project-<n>-concurrent-5-<hash>" is being deleted  failure_reason=runner_system_failure

# The pod-status poll failing, at high volume (1,322 occurrences in the sampled window):
WARNING: Getting job pod status  error=Get "https://<apiserver>/api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/pods/runner-<id>-project-<n>-concurrent-0-<hash>": context canceled
WARNING: Getting job pod status  error=client rate limiter Wait returned an error: context canceled
WARNING: Getting job pod status  error=the server was unable to return a response in the time allotted, but may still be processing the request (get pods runner-<id>-...)

# Informer setup failing, so the executor fell back to polling — including one explicit 429:
WARNING: won't use informers: "SelfSubjectAccessReview creation: the server was unable to return a response in the time allotted", see: https://docs.gitlab.com/runner/executors/kubernetes/#informers
WARNING: won't use informers: "SelfSubjectAccessReview creation: the server has received too many requests", see: https://docs.gitlab.com/runner/executors/kubernetes/#informers

# context deadline exceeded on teardown paths (482 occurrences):
WARNING: Error while executing file based variables removal script  error=context deadline exceeded
WARNING: Error streaming logs <ns>/runner-<id>-.../helper:/logs-<n>/output.log: context deadline exceeded
```
</details>

## Environment description

Custom installation. Kubernetes executor with the attach strategy, on managed Kubernetes. Two production clusters, high-volume CI — tens of thousands of jobs per cluster per day against a shared runner namespace, giving a standing events collection of ~5x10^5 objects.

<details>
<summary> config.toml contents </summary>

```toml
concurrent = 200
check_interval = 10
log_level = "info"

[[runners]]
  executor = "kubernetes"
  request_concurrency = 40
  [runners.feature_flags]
    FF_CONCRETE = false
    # FF_SUSPENDABLE_ENVIRONMENTS not set -> off
  [runners.kubernetes]
    namespace = "<fixed-runner-namespace>"
    namespace_per_job = false
    poll_timeout = 180
    # poll_interval not set -> default 3s
    # print_pod_warning_events not set -> default true
    image = "alpine:latest"
    pull_policy = ["if-not-present"]
    cpu_limit = "4500m"
    memory_limit = "12Gi"
```
</details>

### Used GitLab Runner version

```
Runtime platform    arch=amd64 os=linux pid=1 revision=ac11717a version=19.4.0
```

Rolled back to, and currently running:

```
Runtime platform    arch=amd64 os=linux pid=1 revision=23a5dafc version=19.3.2
```

## Possible fixes

Added by !6781 (`feat(kubernetes): add suspend/resume support via single-PVC overlayfs`), commit `bbcd5520a`.

The call site, in [`getPodPhase` at `util.go:225-229`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/v19.4.0/executors/kubernetes/util.go#L225-229), placed after the early returns for "pod ready" ([`:216`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/v19.4.0/executors/kubernetes/util.go#L216)) and "terminal container error" ([`:221`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/v19.4.0/executors/kubernetes/util.go#L221)), so it runs on every iteration while the pod is pending:

```go
if printPodWarningEvents {
    if err := checkPodSandboxUserNamespaceFailure(ctx, client, pod); err != nil {
        return podPhaseResponse{true, api.PodUnknown, err}
    }
}
```

The function, [`util.go:263-283`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/v19.4.0/executors/kubernetes/util.go#L263-283):

```go
func checkPodSandboxUserNamespaceFailure(ctx context.Context, client kubernetes.Interface, pod *api.Pod) error {
    // kubeAPI: events, list, print_pod_warning_events=true
    events, err := client.CoreV1().Events(pod.Namespace).List(ctx, metav1.ListOptions{
        FieldSelector: fmt.Sprintf("involvedObject.name=%s,type=%s", pod.Name, k8sEventWarningType),
    })
    if err != nil {
        return nil
    }
    ...
}
```

The enclosing poll loop is [`waitForPodRunning`, `util.go:303`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/v19.4.0/executors/kubernetes/util.go#L303).

Two observations from diffing the tags, offered as context rather than as a proposed remedy.

**It is the only new API call in the release not behind a feature flag.** Using the repository's own `// kubeAPI:` annotations, the complete set of call sites added between v19.3.2 and v19.4.0:

```
// kubeAPI: persistentvolumeclaims, create,  FF_SUSPENDABLE_ENVIRONMENTS=true
// kubeAPI: persistentvolumeclaims, delete,  FF_SUSPENDABLE_ENVIRONMENTS=true
// kubeAPI: configmaps, create,              FF_SUSPENDABLE_ENVIRONMENTS=true
// kubeAPI: configmaps, get,                 FF_SUSPENDABLE_ENVIRONMENTS=true
// kubeAPI: configmaps, update,              FF_SUSPENDABLE_ENVIRONMENTS=true
// kubeAPI: configmaps, delete,              FF_SUSPENDABLE_ENVIRONMENTS=true
// kubeAPI: namespaces, get,                 FF_SUSPENDABLE_ENVIRONMENTS=true
// kubeAPI: pods, get,                       FF_CONCRETE=true
// kubeAPI: pods/exec, ...,                  FF_CONCRETE=true
// kubeAPI: pods/log, get,                   FF_CONCRETE=true
// kubeAPI: events, list,                    print_pod_warning_events=true   <-- not a feature flag
```

None were removed. The rest of !6781 is gated behind `FF_SUSPENDABLE_ENVIRONMENTS` and is inert for installations not using it.

**The check cannot match unless suspend/resume is in use.** It looks only for `FailedCreatePodSandBox` events whose message contains `does not support user namespaces`, which requires `spec.hostUsers: false`. `HostUsers` is assigned in exactly one place, [`kubernetes.go:2624`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/v19.4.0/executors/kubernetes/kubernetes.go#L2624), from [`isHostUserEnabled`, `suspend.go:60`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/v19.4.0/executors/kubernetes/suspend.go#L60):

```go
func (s *executor) isHostUserEnabled() *bool {
    if !s.usesSuspendResume() {
        return nil
    }
    return new(false)
}
```

and [`usesSuspendResume`, `suspend.go:338`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/v19.4.0/executors/kubernetes/suspend.go#L338) returns false unless `FF_SUSPENDABLE_ENVIRONMENTS` is enabled **and** the job carries suspend options. With the flag off, `HostUsers` is `nil`, the field is omitted from the pod spec, the kubelet never rejects it, and the event being searched for cannot exist.

Also relevant to any fix: the informer factory, `feature.go` (SelfSubjectAccessReview), and the pod `GET` call site are byte-identical between the two tags, `client-go` is unchanged at v0.36.3, and no retry or QPS/Burst constants changed. This call is the only behavioural difference in the executor's API usage.

**Our mitigation was to roll back to 19.3.2**, which is what we are still running. We have not attempted to run 19.4.0 with `print_pod_warning_events = false`, so we cannot report on whether that is a viable alternative — though from the code the call is unreachable when it is false. Note that one setting also controls the per-poll pod `status.Conditions` output ([`util.go:242-256`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/v19.4.0/executors/kubernetes/util.go#L242-256)) and warning-event retrieval on job failure, so disabling it is not free.

tasks.problem_statement:
GitLab runner system ID is not unique in docker runner

## Summary

The System ID generated by gitlab-runner is supposed to be globally unique. 

However, in practice, we've found that the generated runner ID is both (1) deterministic and (2) the same every time we register a new runner.

This is because the image includes the `/etc/gitlab-runner/.runner_system_id` file, which means a new one will never be generated.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a new container from the image `gitlab/gitlab-runner:v15.8.2`

Find that the contents of `/etc/gitlab-runner/.runner_system_id` are already present and that the value is `r_y3jEhmF8fN58`.

```
docker run --rm -it --entrypoint=""  gitlab/gitlab-runner:v15.8.2 /bin/bash -c "cat /etc/gitlab-runner/.runner_system_id"
```
output:

```
r_y3jEhmF8fN58
```

This behavior is also present in the `latest` image.

## Actual behavior

The system ID is deterministic, even on different systems, in different containers.

## Expected behavior

1. The `.runner_system_id` file should not be present in the gitlab-runner image
2. The generated system ID should be **globally** unique -- that is, it should never (or virtually never) produce the same system ID.


## Relevant logs and/or screenshots

You can see the following two jobs were run on two different runners, which reside on two different physical (EC2) hosts, in different containers. However, both use the same system ID. When running the gitlab-runner image locally, I also see the _same_ ID.

<details>
<summary> screenshots </summary>

![image](/uploads/37a12d9daf3d5bdb585fa1f2f4900ea9/image.png)

![image](/uploads/6e3565724e8eac0c176e293031a8bf2f/image.png)

</details>

## Environment

There aren't really any environment-specific factors here, except for the fact that we do not use docker volume mounts for `/etc/gitlab-runner` on our runners. If a volume mount is used, it will clobber the pre-existing `.runner_system_id` file, avoiding this issue (assuming your mount is unique per system).

## Possible fixes

Ensure the `/etc/gitlab-runner/.runner_system_id` is not present in published docker images.
tasks.short_query: GitLab runner system ID is not unique in docker runner

tasks.problem_statement:
Log network response details on error

# Problem

During [an incident](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/gl-infra/production/-/issues/19438) it was tricky to find the 429 logs that were the cause of runner update failures. We should have a way to know which runner logs correspond with which requests on the gitlab rails side.

@cmcfarland said:

> idea that the runners should log the response codes it gets from talking to the API. Right now, we had to guess what response the API had returned that the runner manager had found to be an error.

- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/gl-infra/production/-/issues/19438#note_2383859631

In the runner logs we saw: 

`json.msg: Job trace termination "Success" failed`

![Screenshot_2025-03-11_at_12.54.40_PM](/uploads/8a07199d2b6a2bd5526808476c92f5fc/Screenshot_2025-03-11_at_12.54.40_PM.png)

This log misses the `path` that was requested and the `status code` and the `response body` that was received back from GitLab. Ci developers are familiar with the status update corresponding to `PUT /api/jobs/:id` but other developers and operators might not be familiar with that. 

This was exacerbated during [the incident](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/gl-infra/production/-/issues/19438) because filtering by `json.method: PUT` `json.path:/api/jobs/:id` on the rails side also did not return the responses since the method is logged inconsistently when the request fails on the rails side at the `RackAttack` layer. https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/183888

# Solution

When the runner fails because an endpoint returns a non 2xx response. Log:

- `path` 
- `status code` 
- `response body` 
- `correlation_id` - in the response as `X-Request-ID` https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/issues/38656#note_2391294283

or any other details that will help associate the runners failure with the rails request type that caused the request to fail.
tasks.short_query: Log network response details on error

tasks.problem_statement:
Docs: Kubernetes overwrite allow lists match any part of the value unless anchored

### Problem to solve

The [Kubernetes executor page](https://docs.gitlab.com/runner/executors/kubernetes/) describes `namespace_overwrite_allowed`, `service_account_overwrite_allowed`, `pod_labels_overwrite_allowed` and `pod_annotations_overwrite_allowed` as a "Regular expression to validate the contents of" the matching overwrite variable, and its settings table has no row for `node_selector_overwrite_allowed` or `node_tolerations_overwrite_allowed`. The page does not say how the expression is matched, and its examples read as if the expression had to match the whole value:

- The [configuration example](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/6ce74c089f2f5bb40861be1c2fdb314cb8871993/docs/executors/kubernetes/_index.md#L446) and the [Overwrite the Kubernetes namespace](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/6ce74c089f2f5bb40861be1c2fdb314cb8871993/docs/executors/kubernetes/_index.md#L2842-2848) section set `namespace_overwrite_allowed = "ci-.*"`, the second one after "To use only designated namespaces during CI runs".
- The [Overwrite the node selector](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/6ce74c089f2f5bb40861be1c2fdb314cb8871993/docs/executors/kubernetes/_index.md#L1948) example sets `node_selector_overwrite_allowed = "kubernetes.io/arch=.*"` to allow "overwrite of the architecture".

The runner compiles the setting as written and accepts a value when `MatchString` finds a match anywhere in it ([`overwriteRegexCheck`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/6ce74c089f2f5bb40861be1c2fdb314cb8871993/executors/kubernetes/overwrites.go#L682-692)). For pod labels, pod annotations, node selectors and node tolerations, it runs that check on the whole variable value before splitting it into key and value ([`evaluateMapOverwrite`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/6ce74c089f2f5bb40861be1c2fdb314cb8871993/executors/kubernetes/overwrites.go#L743-747)). So `ci-.*` also accepts `review-ci-apps`, `kubernetes.io/arch=.*` also accepts `beta.kubernetes.io/arch=amd64`, and an expression written for a label key, such as `^team$`, refuses `team=build`. Anchored with `^` and `$`, `^ci-.*$` and `^kubernetes\.io/arch=.*$` behave as the examples read.

The flag descriptions in `common/config.go`, which `gitlab-runner register --help` prints, say only "Regex to validate", and the [service account one](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/6ce74c089f2f5bb40861be1c2fdb314cb8871993/common/config.go#L780) names `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` instead of `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_OVERWRITE`.

### Further details

No test pins either behaviour. The cases in `executors/kubernetes/overwrites_test.go` use `.*` and patterns that match nothing, and the patterns in `kubernetes_test.go` are anchored in some cases and unanchored in others, but none is tried with a value that it matches only in part.

The page is read by administrators who configure the Kubernetes executor and decide which overwrites a job may request.

### Proposal

Document the existing behaviour, without changing it:

- In the settings table and in each overwrite section, say that the setting is a Go regular expression that matches any part of the value unless it is anchored with `^` and `$`, and that the label, annotation and node selector settings are matched against the whole `key=value` string (the toleration setting against the whole value, effect included).
- Add the missing rows for `node_selector_overwrite_allowed` and `node_tolerations_overwrite_allowed`.
- Anchor the examples. The node selector one is simplest as a TOML literal string, `'^kubernetes\.io/arch=.*$'`, because a basic string reads `\.` as an invalid escape.
- Say that an anchored expression still allows every value it matches, so `^ci-.*$` allows every namespace whose name starts with `ci-`, and that listing names, or `namespace_per_job`, is how to allow only specific namespaces.
- Update the flag descriptions in `common/config.go` and correct the variable name.
- Add unit tests that pin the matching.

Anchoring the expression in code instead would change what existing configurations accept, so I am not proposing it here.

### Who can address the issue

I have a merge request ready that does this.
tasks.short_query: Docs: Kubernetes overwrite allow lists match any part of the value unless anchored

tasks.problem_statement:
Make gitlab-runner pipeline fail when the runner-incept pipeline fails

The `gitlab-runner` pipeline currently ignores failures in the downstream `runner-incept` pipeline. These tests are too important to ignore and failures have been overlooked in the past, leading to regressions going undiscovered for several weeks. Ignoring failing tests can lead to bugs, regression, technical debt, and a loss of trust in our processes. Failing tests should be promptly addressed to ensure reliable, secure, and maintainable code.

Making the `gitlab-runner` pipeline depend on the success of the `runner-incept` pipeline will make it so we have to acknowledge any failures right away. Any ignoring of failures would have to be deliberate on our part.

Example:
Last quarter an [MR to upgrade the BurntSushi/toml version](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/merge_requests/3741) led to [broken runner registration](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/issues/29498). The `runner-incept` pipeline caught this bug right away, but none of us noticed _every_ `runner-incept` pipeline was failing for over 3 weeks.

This may be as simple as setting the [`depend` strategy](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/yaml/index.html#triggerstrategy) in the [trigger job](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/blob/b199f9334194ca86c5edb4b4df4d8c7a222a1cb8/.gitlab/ci/postrelease.gitlab-ci.yml#L9-22).

tasks.problem_statement:
Display an error when service containers are OOM-killed

## Description

When a service consumes more memory than is allowed, the k8s runner does not provide any indication in the runner logs that a service has been OOM-killed by Kubernetes.  From the build container's perspective, the service exists in the hosts file but attempts to connect to it will (understandably) fail.  This makes it difficult to diagnose the problem, as it seems like a configuration/connectivity issue to users who don't have access to the Kubernetes Dashboard to see the "Terminated: OOMKilled" message.

Besides that, the helper container and the corresponding pipeline job continue to run, happily unaware it will be unable to complete its job, until the configured timeout for the pipeline is reached.

## Proposal

Whenever a service is OOMKilled, display an error within the build logs so users are aware this has happened.

Any existing container and pipeline jobs should be terminated when such an event occurs, assuming that the Runner won't be able to recover from losing one of its services to the OOM-killer.

## Links to related issues and merge requests / references

n/a

tasks.problem_statement:
tag gitlab-runner-helper images with CI_RUNNER_VERSION

## Description

When attempting to mirror images to use gitlab-runner in an airgapped environment, it is a burden to have to inspect the Git revision of the gitlab-runner binary in order to figure out which `gitlab-runner-helper` image to mirror so it is available offline.  For the `gitlab-runner` image itself, it *is* tagged with `CI_RUNNER_VERSION` and the image can be determined simply by inspecting the Helm chart.  The `gitlab-runner-helper` image should follow the same pattern.

My values overrides for the chart use this:
```
image: 'docker.knack.works/gitlab/gitlab-runner:alpine-v12.1.0'

runners:
  helpers:
    image: 'docker.knack.works/gitlab/gitlab-runner-helper:x86_64-${CI_RUNNER_REVISION}'
```

But there is no way for me to determine the value of `CI_RUNNER_REVISION` from the Helm chart and need to execute a container instead:
```
docker run -it --rm docker.knack.works/gitlab/gitlab-runner:alpine-v12.1.0 --version | awk -F: '/Git revision/ { print $2 }'
```

## Proposal

The `gitlab-runner-helper` image should also be tagged with `CI_RUNNER_VERSION`.  This would simplify both the mirroring of the images and the values set for the Helm chart because the `gitlab-runner-helper` tag is based on a known value (e.g., v12.1.0).

Alternatively, the value of `CI_RUNNER_REVISION` could be included in the Helm chart so it could be referenced, but that seems like a far worse solution.


## References:
* https://docs.gitlab.com/runner/configuration/advanced-configuration.html#helper-image
* https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/merge_requests/788

tasks.problem_statement:
Long running jobs canceled in GitLab UI, but runner continues process

## Note (revised 2022-04-28)

If you are still experiencing similar issues as described in this issue, then add a comment with your issue details to the [CI process does not receive SIGTERM on termination](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/issues/27443) issue.


## Overview


I have a long running compile job (~40 minutes). I made 2 pushes one after another. I stopped the first running job with the ui. It tells me that the job is canceled. But the second job stays at pending.

I suspect that the runner finishes the job and is not properly terminated. ~~Is there a way to test my hypothesis?~~

I'm using the shell executor for the runner (gitlab and runner are on ubuntu 16.04)

Edit: as written in a comment below steps to reproduce the problem:

create a project with a simple `gitlab-ci.yml` file:

```
build:
  stage: build
  tags:
    - ubuntu_amd64
  script: 
    - ping localhost
```
start a pipeline and cancel it. This should also terminate the ping command (but it doesn't)

on the runner see if the process is still running
```
ps aux | grep ping
gitlab-+ 19828  0.0  0.0   8656  1724 ?        S    07:59   0:00 ping localhost
```
or just kill it with `killall ping` (use `sudo` if the runner is under another user)

## Proposal

At the moment we are simply killing the process group with SIGKILL and then ignore the result. Instead of doing this we should allow the process to gracefully shutdown by first sending `SIGTERM` and after a specific timeout send `SIGKILL` to the process. This will help with the processes being killed properly. We already have this [implemented with the custom executor](https://docs.gitlab.com/runner/executors/custom.html#terminating-and-killing-executables) and should try and reuse the code to implement the same feature.

## Merge Requests

1. [x] [Extract process killer form custom executor](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/merge_requests/1653)
1. [x] [Extract commander interface from custom executor](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/merge_requests/1654)
1. [x] [Add Process groups to `process` pkg](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/merge_requests/1743/)
1. [x] [Use the same termination commands on Windows](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/merge_requests/1797)
    - For windows on the shell executor, we pass [`taskkil`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/blob/cc49cd18e2bd6b071f4c93bef5f0818fc5caf81c/helpers/process_group_windows.go#L16) while in the process package we just call [`process.Kill()`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/blob/cc49cd18e2bd6b071f4c93bef5f0818fc5caf81c/executors/custom/process/killer_windows.go#L33) investigate which one is better or if we should use both.
1. [x] [Rename test file](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/merge_requests/1784) 
1. [x] [Send `SIGTERM` then `SIGKILL` for shell executor](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/merge_requests/1770)


*[Original merge request](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/merge_requests/1551)*
